title: Every nonnegative discrete distribution with zero in its support is an iid-distance law on a complete separable measured metric space
author: Renan Gross
source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue8(2025),1023-1035; DOI10.5802/ahl.254; publisher version
difficulty_reason: Supplying the definition of feasibility and the elementary Bernoulli example leaves a genuinely new inverse construction: the author defines a selection space of eventually constant vectors with the index of last disagreement as distance, and must verify the triangle inequality, completeness, separability and Borel measurability under explicit subadditivity and tail-vanishing hypotheses. The proof then decomposes an arbitrary discrete law into dyadic subdistributions, telescopes the conditional probabilities beta_n so that the total mass of the non-default choices is finite, and matches both the atom at zero and every positive atom exactly. No limit of finite approximations is taken, which is precisely what keeps the space separable; this construction is above ordinary qualification probability and metric geometry.
